Subject: Recap & next steps — quota, bursts, and target unit economics

Hi Susan,

Thanks again for taking time today — good conversation. Quick recap and actionable next steps so we keep momentum: 

What we heard from you
- Primary workload: customer support generation + contextual retrieval augmentation.
- Baseline: ~50M tokens/month across EU + US users.
- Burst behavior: short spikes (1–3 hours) tied to marketing events; peak observed ~2–3M tokens/hour historically.
- Budget target: ~USD 150–200 per 1M tokens (you mentioned aiming at the lower end if possible).

Redwood follow-ups (we will provide):
1) A concise pricing sheet with two commercial paths (Hosted, Dedicated commit) and explicit overage math. (attached: redwood_pricing-draft.xlsx)
2) A short note on rate-limit behavior and burst handling: how soft limits, burst token buckets, and emergency quota increases work.
3) An example unit-econ calc showing cost at baseline vs. 2x/3x burst scenarios so you can see $/1M impact.

Immediate asks for you (to finalize options):
- Share a 7-day peak snapshot (CSV or S3 link) showing highest 1-hour token rates and daily totals (helps sizing).
- Confirm procurement timeline and whether your Finance/Procurement team prefers PO-first or DocuSign route.

Tentative next steps & owners
- Ben (me): send updated pricing & burst policy by EOD tomorrow.
- Karthik: follow up with a technical note on per-route rate limits and per-tenant burst config.
- Neha: stand by for a short demo of the quota/insights dashboard if you want to see real telemetry.

If the 150–200/1M target is firm, we’ll prioritize options that get you closer to that via committed volume (Dedicated) or multi-month discounts.

Thanks — I’ll attach the draft and follow up tomorrow with the concrete numbers.

Best,
Ben Carter

Subject: Internal: Proposal options + quick math (sharing with Susan)

Karthik / Neha — looped you in on the thread. Drafting two clear commercial options aligned to Susan’s numbers. I’ll share these with Susan and procurement as soon as we align internally. High level: 

Option A — Hosted (fastest start)- Monthly quota: 60M tokens (covers baseline + small growth).
- Price: USD 200 per 1M tokens (list for low-commit hosted).
- Burst handling: soft rate limit with token bucket allowing up to 3x baseline for short windows; 10% free burst buffer before overage billing.
- Overage: billed at USD 240 per 1M tokens when quota exceeded for >1 continuous hour (billed daily, prorated).
- Advantages: no commit, quick onboarding.

Option B — Dedicated (commit)- Commit: 36-month or 12-month term options; recommend 12-month to start.
- Monthly commit: 50M tokens.
- Effective price: USD 140 per 1M tokens at 50M commit; priced down to ~USD 120 per 1M with 80M+ commit.
- Burst policy: baseline quota + configurable surge buffer up to 2x commit for short intervals (1–4 hours) automatically allowed; excess beyond the burst buffer triggers negotiated overage rate (USD 160 per 1M).
- Advantages: predictable unit economics, lower $/1M at scale, SLA-backed latency targets.

Quick unit-econ example (from Susan's snapshot):
- Baseline 50M @ $140/1M (Dedicated example) => monthly cost = (50 * 140) = $7,000.
- 3M token 90-min burst = 3 * $140 = $420 (if within committed buffer); if overage rate applies at $160/1M => $480.

Rate-limit / overage mechanics to note:
- Soft limit vs hard quota: soft limits allow requests through and meter; hard quota stops requests. We prefer soft by default for user-facing apps.
- Burst allowance: configurable per-API route; we can set higher token-buckets for support endpoints.
- Automatic quota increase: short-term emergency auto-increase possible (technical + commercial guardrails) — typically requires pre-approved spend threshold and is subject to billing/PO confirmation.
- SLOs: latency SLOs vary by model class; can include uptime & latency credits in Dedicated deals.

Action: I will send the customer-facing proposal with explicit examples and DocuSign-ready terms by 10/14. Karthik — can you add the per-route rate-limit spec? Neha — prepare a console demo for telemetry.

Ben

Thanks — useful framing. A couple of clarifying questions before we take this to procurement: 
1) You mention a 10% free burst buffer for Hosted — is that 10% of monthly quota or a 10% immediate allowance for short windows? How is that enforced?
2) For Dedicated overage at USD 160/1M, is there a daily cap on overage exposure or do you require a pre-approved spend threshold before automatic increases?
3) SLA credits — can you share a short sample SLA for Dedicated (latency & availability) we can evaluate?

We prefer a default soft-limit behavior (we can risk meter vs. hard reject) but procurement will want clear guardrails on runaway cost. If you can confirm the answers and send a one-page summary + a DocuSign-ready quote, procurement is ready to review next week.

— Susan

Susan / Procurement — quick answers and next artifacts attached: one-pager (pricing + burst rules) and DocuSign draft.

Answers: 
- 10% free burst buffer: this is 10% of the monthly quota that can be used as short-term overflow without triggering overage charges; enforced as a rolling 24-hour allowance measured against your quota. Practically: with a 60M quota you get a 6M token buffer that clears/refreshes across the month.
- Overage exposure & caps: we offer two behaviors: (A) automatic soft bump up to a pre-approved spend cap (you set a $/day or $/month threshold), or (B) hard guardrail that blocks additional requests after quota is exceeded. For commercial proposals we typically set a default daily spend cap (e.g., $2,000/day) unless you prefer blocking.
- SLA sample: attached one-pager includes an example latency SLO and availability target for Dedicated; we can include explicit SLA credit language in the contract.

Attachments: 
- Redwood_pricing_onepager.pdf (pricing + burst rules summary)
- RDW-RD-5234-proposal-docusign.pdf (DocuSign-ready quote)

Next steps: 
1) Review with procurement — if DocuSign route works, I will issue the DocuSign link and route to legal.
2) If procurement wants a PO-first approach, send PO to billing@redwood.ai and we’ll provision after PO acceptance.
3) Karthik / Neha: please prepare the short SLA & per-route limit doc and a 15-minute console demo link for next week.

If that works I’ll queue the DocuSign draft now.

Best,
Ben
